_README: The Release workflow: build, test, archive, TestFlight. Companion to ci-workflow.example.json
(the PR Gate). Same script: `create-xcode-cloud-workflow.sh create <this file>`.
Fill the four <...> ids from the discovery subcommands. The script strips this key before POSTing.
THE ONE-WAY DOOR — read before creating this workflow:
'buildDistributionAudience' MUST be 'APP_STORE_ELIGIBLE'.
'INTERNAL_ONLY' stamps every uploaded build buildAudienceType: INTERNAL_ONLY, permanently
and immutably. Such a build reaches internal testers and can NEVER be added to an external
group — its externalBuildState is NOT_APPLICABLE and there is no undo. A sibling project
stranded thirteen builds this way by choosing the cautious-looking option during setup.
App Store Connect gives no useful signal: the external add-build picker just says 'No builds
available', and the real reason is visible only via the iris/v1/builds/<id> API.
APP_STORE_ELIGIBLE still distributes to internal testers. It costs nothing and keeps the
external path open. There is no reason to choose INTERNAL_ONLY.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE WORKFLOW FROM THE GATE (ADR-004): archiving on every pull request
costs minutes and produces builds nobody installs. The gate proves; this ships.
TEST BEFORE ARCHIVE, both isRequiredToPass: a red suite must stop the upload rather than
ship past it. Action order in this array is the execution order.
BUILD NUMBERS: ci_post_clone.sh stamps CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION from $CI_BUILD_NUMBER before
XcodeGen runs, because the archive takes CFBundleVersion from the generated project and not
from the environment variable. Creating this workflow makes that stamping load-bearing, and
makes Cloud the sole owner of the build number. A local archive during Cloud's tenure needs
the number reconciled deliberately or App Store Connect rejects the duplicate.
NOT YET VERIFIED — reconcile on first run: the ANY_MAC destination, and whether a macOS
archive needs a distinct action shape from the iOS one. The iOS values are confirmed.
